-- (The hover/completion helpers below are DELIBERATELY reimplemented from the
--  same logic in compiler/tools/lsp.mdk rather than shared: importing lsp.mdk
--  into this entry drags in tools.fmt + io and trips a pre-existing multi-module
--  flat-union type conflation ("Token vs a -> b" at lsp.mdk's nextMode).  The
--  duplication is the cost of keeping this entry's module graph small + correct.)
-- playground_main.mdk — COMBINED diagnostics + WasmGC-emit entry for the
-- server-free in-browser Medaka playground (Stage 2).
--
-- WHY this entry exists
-- ---------------------
-- The bare emit entry (entries/wasm_emit_modules_main.mdk), when fed a
-- type-broken or parse-broken program, compiles its native diagnostic/panic path
-- to a wasm `unreachable` trap that aborts with ZERO bytes on stdout/stderr — so
-- a browser host cannot surface compile errors through it.  This entry runs the
-- REAL front end (the same `analyzeLocated`/`analyzeProject` path the native
-- `medaka check --json` uses), and:
--   * if there are check errors → prints JSON diagnostics in the SAME shape
--     `medaka check --json` emits ({"files":[{"file","diagnostics":[...]}]}),
--     then exits 0 cleanly — NO trap;
--   * if clean → emits the program's WAT (exactly as wasm_emit_modules_main does).
-- Because emit runs only AFTER a clean analyze, a well-typed program never reaches
-- the emit-panic path.
--
-- HOW MANY TIMES IT RUNS (S2/#2442 — this line used to read "ONCE" and was wrong).
-- Per invocation, over the user's program:
--   `analyze` — parsed + loaded ONCE (`run`'s `loadProgramFilesLocatedCachedE`, threaded downstream),
--     typechecked ONCE (`analyzeFrom`/`analyzeProject`); PLUS one further check of
--     the SYNTHETIC auto-print wrap (`underivedMainDiags`) on the bare-value mains
--     that trigger it, which is a different program and not a repeat of the same
--     work.
--     Prelude parsing+desugaring goes through the process-wide content-keyed
--     `desugaredPrelude` memo (`frontend/desugar_cache.mdk`) on BOTH arms —
--     `analyzeFrom` on the single-module arm, `analyzeProject` on the
--     multi-module arm — so `doEmit`'s reads below are cache hits either way,
--     and, because the host re-enters `main` on one live instance
--     (`mdk_main`, see playground/compile.mjs), the prelude is parsed and
--     desugared once per SESSION, not once per keystroke.  User modules are
--     loaded through the loader's source-keyed parse memo, likewise held for
--     the session (`playgroundParseCache`).
--   `compile` — all of the above, plus exactly one emit-side `elaborateModules`
--     inside `runEmit`.
-- Before S2 this entry additionally re-loaded and re-parsed every user module, re-parsed
-- and re-desugared runtime.mdk + core.mdk, and ran a whole extra `elaborateModules`
-- whose result it threw away — ~161ms and ~99ms respectively of a 454ms `analyze` of a
-- four-line program, measured on the Node driver.
--
-- ARG CONTRACT (identical to wasm_emit_modules_main):
--   <runtime.mdk> <core.mdk> <entry.mdk> [root ...]
--   (roots default to [dirOf entry] when omitted)
--
-- OUTPUT-MARKER PROTOCOL (first line of stdout is the marker, rest is payload):
--   __MEDAKA_DIAGNOSTICS__\n<one-line JSON {"files":[...]}>\n        ← had check errors
--   __MEDAKA_WAT__\n<the WAT text>                                  ← clean, no warnings
--   __MEDAKA_WAT_DIAGS__\n<one-line JSON {"files":[...]}>\n<WAT>     ← clean but WARNINGS
-- present (e.g. W-NONEXHAUSTIVE): warnings never block emit (they don't in native
-- `medaka check` either), so the WAT still follows the warnings JSON line — the
-- caller shows the warnings AND runs the program.
-- The caller (playground/compile.mjs) splits on newlines: the marker line selects
-- the branch; for __MEDAKA_WAT_DIAGS__ the SECOND line is the warnings JSON and
-- everything after that is the WAT. Diagnostics JSON is byte-identical to
-- `medaka check --json` (the cj* renderers below mirror medaka_cli.mdk).
--   __MEDAKA_ANALYZE__\n<one-line JSON {"files":[...]}>\n         ← `analyze` mode
-- (diagnostics only, no codegen): no ERROR diagnostics.  The JSON line carries the
-- same warnings `__MEDAKA_WAT_DIAGS__` would have carried, or `{"files":[]}` when
-- there are none — `analyze` ALWAYS prints a marker AND a payload, so the host
-- never has to tell "clean" apart from "no output".  Errors under `analyze` use
-- `__MEDAKA_DIAGNOSTICS__`, byte-identically to `compile`.
--
-- This entry is OUTSIDE the self-host compiler graph (an entry, not imported), so
-- it needs no fixpoint/seed: the decisive checks are wasm-tools assemble/validate
-- plus the Node round-trip.  It composes EXISTING analyze + emit functions; only
-- the thin cj* JSON shaping is reproduced (those live in medaka_cli.mdk, which is
-- itself an entry and cannot be imported).

-- PARAMETRIC heads (#781, S0): a parametric impl head (`impl Sig (List a)`) is never
  -- reached by the ground filter, so a genuine non-literal type mismatch inside its
  -- method body (`sig _ = idInt "str"`, `idInt : Int -> Int` in a String-returning
  -- method) went unenforced end-to-end — `check`/`build` exit 0 and the built binary
  -- printed a wrong value.  Infer these bodies too so the `unify`/`typeMismatch` clash
  -- is surfaced (it is pushed to `typeErrors`, and kept because nothing removes it —
  -- see the retirement note at the end of this function), mirroring the
  -- ground-head fix.  BUT a parametric impl also records obligations on its ABSTRACT
  -- element tyvar (`impl Eq (List a) requires Eq a` → an `Eq a` obligation over an
  -- unground var); those never ground on the check path and would reach
  -- checkUndeterminedObligation as a SPURIOUS `Ambiguous instance` for any iface with
  -- >= 2 impls (it fired on every program the moment core's own parametric impls were
  -- inferred — the prelude snapshot).  So WINDOW the obligation channel across this
  -- pass and restore it afterward: the body-clash errors go through `typeErrors`, NOT
  -- the obligation channel, so windowing keeps the #781 reject while dropping the
  -- abstract-var false positives.
  --
  -- 🚨 #1114 (#792): THE ROLLBACK IS GROUND-PRESERVING, and it did not used to be.
  -- The two `wRestore`s below used to run bare, which threw away EVERY obligation the
  -- parametric pass recorded — including the GROUND ones, which are exactly the ones
  -- the abstract-var argument above does not cover.  `impl Foo (List a)` whose body
  -- calls `debug Bar` records a fully-ground `Debug Bar`; nothing about it is abstract,
  -- the gate would have rejected it on the spot, and the blanket rollback deleted it —
  -- so `check` exited 0 while `build` PANICKED (`no impl of method 'debug' for type
  -- 'Bar'`).  That is a `run_check_agreement` break, and the sentence this comment
  -- replaced ("stays deferred to `build` exactly as before — a residual, not a
  -- regression") named it as a known residual without naming its cost.
  --
  -- The policy is now written down: DICT-SEMANTICS §4.2 **D1** (a predicate the gate can
  -- decide where it is recorded is discharged there — no window may discard it) and
  -- **D6(b)** (a window that exists to suppress D3 false positives must filter by what is
  -- DECIDABLE, not discard wholesale).  So: window as before, then re-push exactly the
  -- obligations `uOblIsDecidableNow` accepts.  The abstract element tyvar of a parametric
  -- head is decidable by nothing, so every false positive the window was built to stop is
  -- still stopped.
  --
  -- ⚠️ The predicate is "the GATE can decide it now", NOT "it is ground" — those differ,
  -- and this site is where believing otherwise costs a verdict.  `uOblIsDecidableNow`
  -- carries the derivation and the counterexample (`Debug (Int -> Int)`); read it before
  -- touching either side.
  -- Re-pushed in `reverseL` order because `wWindow` yields newest-first (items are
  -- consed): reversing restores the original record order, which the gate reports in.

-- #412: the PREDICATE-keyed half of the given registry.  `activeDictVars` above is keyed
-- by TYVAR ID, which cannot express a STRUCTURED given: `requires S (List a)` registers
-- only `a`'s id (monoTyvarIds descends to the leaves), and the goal `S (List a)` looks up
-- through `activeDictVarOf`, which recurses to the SPINE HEAD (`TCon "List"`) and finds no
-- tyvar — so `assum` was unreachable by construction and `entail` fell through to
-- `entailInst`, statically committing the body to the GENERAL instance and discarding the
-- most-specific dict the construction site had correctly built and passed.  DICT-SEMANTICS
-- §3 (assum before inst) + :155-166 (sub-evidence is never pre-baked at the declaration).
-- Keyed by (iface, WHOLE argument vector) so it is neither iface-blind nor
-- structure-blind, and matched by `monoVecSameGiven` — pointwise `monoSameGiven`,
-- structural, on rigid-tyvar IDENTITY, never unification.
--
-- 🚨 #1956 / #1937: THE KEY IS THE VECTOR, NOT THE LEAD ARGUMENT.  This arm used to
-- match `[subject]` and return `()` for any longer vector, so a MULTI-PARAMETER
-- declared context (`f : Conv (Wrap a) b => …`) had no consumption-side answer at all:
-- `entailAssum` could never see it, `entail` fell through to `entailInst`, and the body
-- was statically committed to whichever impl was most specific at ABSTRACTION time while
-- the caller's correctly-built dict went unread — so `f (Wrap 5) True` and `f (Wrap 'c')
-- 7` both took the SAME impl, and swapping the two `impl` blocks changed which one, at
-- exit 0 (DICT-SEMANTICS §3 forbids selection by declaration order outright).
-- ⚠️ THE ANSWER TO "when are two predicate argument vectors the same predicate?" IS
-- POINTWISE STRUCTURAL IDENTITY OVER THE VECTOR: equal length, and `monoSameGiven` at
-- every position, in order.  `goalMatchesGiven`/`goalSlotStillOpen` follow this shape
-- exactly, and must keep following it — see their own headers.
--
-- §6.1.3's rigid commit is preserved TWICE OVER, and the guard below is the load-bearing
-- one: `requires S a` is a bare-tyvar given, so this writer registers nothing for it, and
-- the body's goal `S (List a)` finds no assumption ⇒ `inst` fires on the rigid goal ⇒ the
-- general instance ⇒ 2, unchanged.  Even had it been registered, `monoSameGiven` compares
-- structurally and would not match subject `a` against goal `List a` — only unification
-- would, and this is deliberately not unification.  Pinned by
-- test/build_diff_fixtures/impl_requires_structured_rigid_control.mdk.
--
-- #2547 unit 3: the guard is a `GivenMatch` decision now, not an absence.  The
-- all-bare vector this arm refuses IS in `gGiven` — `registerReqSlots` pushes it as
-- `GMIdWitnessed` — and what preserves the paragraph above is that every reader keyed on
-- predicate identity alone scans `GSPredicateOnly` and so cannot see it.  Both halves must
-- move together: pushing an all-bare vector as `GMPredicate`, or widening a
-- `GSPredicateOnly` rung, re-opens exactly what this guard closes.  Function carriers have
-- a distinct Known-slot writer (`registerSlotPredGivens`) because their complete
-- multi-parameter identity is required by EKNestedTop.
--
-- ⚠️ #1956 WIDENS THAT SHARP EDGE TO MORE POSITIONS, and does not introduce a new one.
-- A vector like `[Wrap a, b]` is admitted because SOME position is structured, but its
-- SECOND position is a bare tyvar matched by raw id — the same `TVar`/`TVar` arm of
-- `monoSameGiven`, one position over.  The structured position still gates the whole
-- match (all positions must agree, so a stale-id coincidence at a bare position can only
-- matter for a goal that already agrees structurally elsewhere at the same interface),
-- which is why this is a widening of an existing hazard rather than a new one.  Removing
-- it is the same scoped-projection question `activeDictVarOf`'s `inImpl` gate answers,
-- and belongs with the key-side work (#1904), not here.
comments.code_after:
registerPredGiven : IfaceRef -> List Mono -> EvidenceBinderId -> Unit
registerPredGiven _ [] _ = ()
registerPredGiven iface args dname
  | allList monoIsBareTyvar args = ()
  | otherwise =
    let slot = PredicateSlot {
      psIface = iface,
      psArgs = PSArgsKnown args,
      psBoundIds = dedupI (flatMap monoTyvarIds args),
    }
    pushGiven GMPredicate DirectGiven slot dname

comments.comment:
-- ── owning-package rebasing for a dep's intra-package imports ─────────────────
--
-- When a module is loaded from a dependency package (`owningRoot` ≠ the entry
-- root), its OWN imports must resolve against THAT package, not the entry
-- project:
--   * its intra-package (relative/bare) imports — `import lib.parser`,
--     `import foo` — rebase to `owningRoot` (prepended to `roots` so the dep's
--     copy is preferred over a same-named entry-project module);
--   * its OWN `[dependencies]` (a transitive dep — a dep importing ITS dep by
--     name) become visible by reading `<owningRoot>/medaka.toml`'s deps and
--     appending them.  The entry's deps stay first so the entry's view wins on a
--     name clash, and a dep's stdlib imports keep flowing through the original
--     `roots` (the stdlib root is never dropped).
--
-- 🚨 The rebase is UNCONDITIONAL — `owningRoot` is prepended even when it is
-- ALREADY in `roots`.  It must not be guarded by `contains owningRoot roots`
-- ("nothing changes for a module found under a root we already have"): that
-- guard silently exempts the two roots it matters most for: the STDLIB root and
-- the entry project root, both of which are ALWAYS in `roots`.  `roots` is
-- ordered entry-dir-FIRST (`[entryDir, projRoot, stdlibDir]` on the check/run
-- path), so under the guard a stdlib module's OWN `import list as L` searched the
-- USER'S entry directory first.  A user file that merely happens to be named
-- `list.mdk` next to the entry point then hijacked `stdlib/hash_map.mdk`'s private
-- view of `list` and broke the STDLIB from the outside — on a program that never
-- mentions `list` at all:
--   `stdlib/hash_map.mdk:305:14: Unbound variable: L.sortOn`
-- `test/build_diff_fixtures/list.mdk` is exactly such a file, which is why
-- `deriving_hashable.mdk` and `hash_negative_hash.mdk` (its neighbours, both
-- reaching `hash_map`) could neither be checked nor built in that directory.
-- Prepending unconditionally states the actual rule — A MODULE'S OWN IMPORTS
-- RESOLVE AGAINST ITS OWN PACKAGE FIRST — for every package, the stdlib and the
-- entry project included.  Regression legs: `diff_compiler_check_cli_modules.sh`
-- leg 19.
--
-- ⚠️ PREPEND ONLY, NEVER MOVE.  `owningRoot`'s EXISTING position in `roots` must
-- be left alone: `canonRootFor` (above) measures a module id from the LAST root
-- containing the file, and that "stdlib LAST" ordering is what keeps `list`
-- spelled `list` rather than `stdlib.list` when the stdlib lives inside the
-- project tree.  Deleting the old occurrence while prepending would invert
-- exactly that, renaming every stdlib id under a `src/`-layout project.  So the
-- head is a resolution-order override; the tail stays the canonicalization order.
-- Skipping the cons when `owningRoot` is already the head keeps the list from
-- lengthening once per DFS level (every extra root costs a `fileExists` probe per
-- import in `findInRoots`): a same-package descent — the overwhelmingly common
-- case, and every step of a stdlib or compiler subtree — adds nothing at all.
comments.code_after:
childRoots : String -> List String -> List String
childRoots owningRoot [] = [owningRoot]
childRoots owningRoot (r :: rs) =
  if r == owningRoot then r :: rs else owningRoot :: r :: rs

comments.comment:
-- `record` has been removed as a declaration keyword (records are now the
-- `data X = { … }` short form), but — unlike `mut`/`function` above — the WORD
-- is an ordinary identifier again (#62; `keywordOrIdent`, lexer.mdk, carries the
-- reasoning for the split).  So this scan can no longer key on the token: it
-- keys on the removed CONSTRUCT'S SHAPE, the same way `firstForeignKwIdx` keys
-- on `for`/`while`/`def` (also plain `TIdent`s).
--
-- Shape: a TOP-LEVEL logical line that starts `record Upper` (after any
-- `export`/`public` modifier) and then either
--   (a) has a depth-0 `=` followed by `{` — allowing ONE `INDENT`/`NEWLINE`
--       between them, which is how the multi-line form lexes — with no `|` at
--       that brace's own depth before its `}`; or
--   (b) reaches the end of its logical line with NO depth-0 `=` at all, having
--       seen a depth-0 `:` or such a `{`.
--
-- Arm (b) is not an extra: it is the form
-- `docs/spec/language-design.md` still documents as THE product-type syntax —
--     record Person
--       name : String
--       age  : Int
-- — which lexes as ONE logical line (`Person` `canEndExpr`, so the deeper lines
-- are absorbed as application continuations and no INDENT is ever emitted), and
-- is therefore the shape a reader migrating from that doc actually types.  It
-- was diagnosed on `main` by the old bare-token scan; dropping it here would
-- have traded a precise removal message for `unexpected ':'` on the wrong line.
--
-- SAFETY (why this can never fire on valid Medaka).  Two independent proofs,
-- one per arm.
--
-- (a) A `{` that STARTS an expression has exactly one production in this
-- grammar — `parseRecordUpdate` (`parseAtomRaw`'s `TLBrace =>
-- parseRecordUpdate`), which is `{ expr | field = val, … }` and therefore
-- ALWAYS contains a `|` at the brace's own depth (it `expectTok TPipe`
-- unconditionally).  A constructor record literal (`P { x = 1 }`) has no `|`,
-- but it is `TUpper`-led (`upperAtomRest c TLBrace`), so its `{` is never the
-- token right after `=`.  Hence `= {` with no depth-1 `|` is not a parseable
-- expression under any arm.  Verified on the binary: `f Point = { x : Int, y :
-- Int }` fails with `unexpected ','; expected '|'`, while `f Pat = { r | x = 1
-- }` and `f Pat = P { x = 1 }` both compile — and neither matches this shape,
-- one-line or multi-line (the `|` is inside the braces either way).
--
-- (b) A top-level declaration line ALWAYS contains a depth-0 `=`, unless it is
-- a type signature — and a signature's LHS is a single lowercase name, so it
-- cannot be `record Upper …`.  Every other decl form starts with its own
-- keyword (`data`/`interface`/`impl`/`import`/…), not with an identifier.  So
-- "starts `record Upper` and has no depth-0 `=` on the whole logical line" is
-- already never-valid on its own; the `:`/`{` evidence is required on top of
-- that only to keep the RECORD message off unrelated broken lines.
--
-- The `Upper` requirement keeps the scan off ordinary code that merely binds
-- the name (`record = 1`, `record r = { r | x = 1 }`, `record : Int`): the
-- removed construct always named an uppercase type.  Located at `record`, not
-- at the modifier — that is the word the message is about.

-- C8b: type-check ALL interface default bodies, unconditionally.
--
-- Constrained arm (non-empty ids): method has method-level constraints (e.g. foldMap : Monoid m =>):
--   Instantiate scheme, register constraint vars → dict param names (for dict-passing
--   emit path), infer body, unify.

--   from the SAME sigToSchemeTvs build of THIS method's type.  Reading the ids from
--   methodPredicateSlotsRef (filled by a separate method-row build with its own
--   fresh tyvar ids) and instantiating an unrelated methodSchemesPure scheme gave ids
--   that did not appear in the instantiation subst → registerOneMethodDict's
--   `lookupAssocI id subst` returned None → activeDictVars got no entry → the in-body
--   `empty`/`++` routed RNone → eval's `++` saw a non-monoid acc and panicked
--   ('++' requires Semigroup).  This code path
--   uses ONE method_schemes build for both.
--
-- Unconstrained arm (empty ids): method has no method-level constraints (e.g. Ord.lt):
--   Instantiate scheme, infer body, unify — same but no dict registration.

-- result against the declared type would add a `Method '<m>': …` line that blames the
-- victim.  NORMATIVE HOME: `compiler/ERROR-QUALITY.md` §3 dim R ("Pinpoints the single

-- removed 2026-06-26, so the citation named nothing; the rule is ours now, and its
-- conformance fixture is `test/typecheck_error_fixtures/iface_default_dedup_cascade.mdk`
-- (which pins the shared KEYING; it does not on its own discriminate this gate — that
-- would need a compiler built with S1 removed, and nobody has built one).
--
-- ⚠️ THE GATED BLOCK IS NOT DIAGNOSTICS-ONLY.  `unify expected2 actualTy` mutates
-- union-find state that `defaultBodyLocalNum` reads below — its job (#873) is grounding
-- body-local `Num` vars so the right impl is selected — so skipping it moves GROUNDING,
-- hence dispatch, not just what prints.  On the ordinary path that is harmless because
-- a detection here means the program is rejected anyway; across the check drivers'

-- `# TYPES_USER` — the PRELUDE-AWARE user-only variant.  `# TYPES` above is
-- prelude-FREE (`checkOneToLinesWithRuntime runtimeDecls [] d`): correct for the minimal
-- typecheck_fixtures (which test errors *without* a prelude in scope), but WRONG for a
-- real program that references prelude types — every prelude reference would be an
-- unbound-name error.  This variant typechecks `coreDecls ++ d` (prelude in scope) so
-- the user schemes infer correctly, then keeps ONLY the user program's own bindings.
--
-- WHY name-filter, not `full − prelude_baseline` (measured): a prelude function whose
-- inferred scheme is context-sensitive (`abs : a -> a` under ambiguous-Num defaulting
-- resolves differently per fixture) does NOT cancel against a fixed prelude baseline and
-- LEAKS in as a false user line.  Keying on the NAME is exact: keep a scheme line iff its
-- binding name is a user binding — `funNamesOf d` (the DESUGARED user decls, so
-- deriving-generated functions are covered) PLUS user `extern` names (`externNamesOf`): an
-- extern is a top-level user binding that DOES appear in the scheme dump (`kvGet : String
-- -> <KV> String`), so `funNamesOf` alone is NOT the complete user set.  User data
-- CONSTRUCTORS, by contrast, never appear in the scheme dump (it is top-level value
-- bindings — functions + externs — only).  A user binding that SHADOWS a prelude name is
-- in the user set, so its (user) scheme is kept.  See

-- compiler/types/typecheck.mdk is LOCKED by ws:typecheck.

-- `TYPE ERROR:` lines instead of a scheme dump (whole run bypasses the filter); and match
-- warnings are appended to the scheme dump as `Warning:` prose, kept by `isDiagProse`
-- regardless of any ` : ` a future message might contain.  Both must survive so the
-- section still reports the diagnostic (and stays unblessable).

-- Per-parameter variance, inferred from constructor field occurrences.  Mirrors
-- `inferParamKinds`' shape: one pass over `payloadAstTypes`, positional result.
--
-- ⚠️ ORDER-SENSITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, AND IT UNDER-TIGHTENS ON A MISS.  A
-- `TyApp` spine composes the occurrence's own polarity with the HEAD type's
-- recorded polarity at that slot, so `data Cell a = MkCell (Ref a)` needs
-- `Ref`'s row to already be visible.  A CONCRETE head that is not yet
-- registered — a forward reference, or the type itself, as in `data List a =
-- Nil | Cons a (List a)` — reads `PCo` (`polarityAtOr None`), which is exactly
-- today's (fully lenient) behaviour: it can only fail to tighten, never reject
-- something that used to be accepted.  That default is what makes the
-- self-recursive `List` come out `PCo`, and `declEnvPolarityEntriesFix`
-- iterates it away for everything but genuine self-recursion.
-- 🚨 THAT PARAGRAPH SCOPES TO THE UNREGISTERED-*TyCon*-HEAD MISS ONLY, AND IS
-- NOT THE ABSTRACT-HEAD ARM (#2107).  The two were one sentence until #2107
-- separated them: a head that is a type *parameter* (`data W f a = MkW (f a)`)
-- can never become registered by iterating, because its polarity is not a fact
-- about this declaration at all — it depends on what `f` is instantiated to at
-- each use.  See that arm's own note in `paramOccPolarities` below.
-- ⚠️ THE TABLE IT COMPOSES AGAINST IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT `perRun`, and that is
-- load-bearing: `declEnvPolarityChain` runs this over the WHOLE import graph
-- while building the cross-module seed, at a point where the per-run ref holds
-- nothing yet.  Reading the ref here would have made cross-module transitivity
-- silently lenient while the single-file path tightened — the split
-- `[WT-multi-module-check]` names.
comments.code_after:
inferParamPolarities : List (TabKey, List Polarity) ->
  List String ->
  List Variant ->
  List Polarity
inferParamPolarities tab params variants =
  let fieldTys = flatMap (v => payloadAstTypes (variantPayload v)) variants
  map
    (p =>
      joinPolarities (flatMap (t => paramOccPolarities tab p PCo t) fieldTys))
    params

-- #1867 + PERF (#1974): the ONE call-obligation verdict, answered from ONE pair of
-- bucket lookups.  It fuses two questions the separate `oblGoalIsTruncated` /
-- `implMatchesArgsU` pair asked over THE SAME buckets, each re-minting (and re-RENDERING,
-- see `insertUnivImplAt`) its registry key:
--   `None`       — the goal is a TRUNCATION of a k-parameter predicate, k > its own
--                  arity: some impl of [iface] this goal could reach declares more head
--                  types than the goal carries.  Scoped to arity 1 because that is the
--                  only truncation any producer mints — `recordCallObligations` shatters
--                  a predicate into ONE obligation per dict slot, each carrying a single
--                  mono; every other goal on this channel is a whole vector.  See
--                  `checkOneCallObligation`'s block for the verdict this decides and why
--                  deferring is not a [W-QUIETER] regression.
--   `Some True`  — some impl matches (receiver-only at arity 1, full head vector above).
--   `Some False` — no impl matches.
-- ⚠️ ORDER IS SEMANTIC AND UNCHANGED.  The truncation question is still asked FIRST and
-- over BOTH buckets (concrete receiver-head bucket, then the iface's headless bucket) —
-- a goal that is truncated defers even when the concrete bucket would have matched it.
-- The headless bucket is still read only when the concrete one did not already answer
-- "truncated", exactly as the old `||` short-circuited; it is then REUSED by the match
-- test instead of being looked up again.  No third universe, no new registry read.
comments.code_after:
oblCallVerdict : ImplUniverse -> IfaceRef -> List Mono -> Option Bool
oblCallVerdict univ iface [a0] =
  let cb = univConcreteBucket univ iface (headTyconMono a0)
  if bucketAnyLonger cb 1 then
    None
  else
    let hb = univHeadless univ iface
    if bucketAnyLonger hb 1 then
      None
    else
      Some (bucketRecvMatch cb a0 || bucketRecvMatch hb a0)
oblCallVerdict univ iface args = Some (implMatchesU univ iface args)

-- ── capture-free closure hoisting (S-1, EMITTER-GAPS #10 allocation half) ───
-- THE SPRINT'S MECHANISM.  A closure cell whose capture set is EMPTY has fields
-- that are ALL compile-time constants: the header is the literal arity and field 0
-- is `ptrtoint (ptr @mdk_lamN to i64)`, already a constant-expression.  Such a cell
-- is immutable and identical at every entry to the enclosing function, so it does
-- NOT need a per-entry `@mdk_alloc`: emit it ONCE as an `internal constant` module
-- global and use `ptrtoint (ptr @g to i64)` as the closure word.  Exactly the
-- transform `emitConstDictCell` already performs for constant dict witnesses, and
-- byte-identical in LAYOUT to `emitClosureCell`'s heap cell (header at offset 0,
-- field i at 8*(i+1)) so every consumer — `loadField` code-ptr load, `__mdk_apply`,
-- a capture-word store into a sibling cell — reads it unchanged.
--
-- SOUND because a closure cell is READ-ONLY after construction on this path: the
-- only writer is the knot-tying back-patch (`knotPatch`), and mutual/forward groups
-- are routed to `emitLetGroupKnot` BEFORE reaching here (F9 — an immutable global
-- cannot be back-patched, so that path keeps its per-entry alloc by design).
-- `__mdk_apply` only reads the cell; a PAP is a separate freshly-allocated cell.
--
-- Cached by `constCellKey` in its own cache (NOT `dictConstCache` — different
-- value domain, and sharing it would let a dict and a closure alias one global).
-- ⚠️ In practice this cache can never HIT: `lamName` is always minted from
-- `freshId` at the call site (`emitGroupBind`'s `mdk_lam.<scope>.<id>`,
-- `emitLamGo`'s and `emitLamPat`'s own for a capture-free user lambda, each
-- eta-wrapper's `mdk_eta_<name>.<scope>.<id>` / `mdk_etac_<name>.<scope>.<id>`),
-- so `initBody`'s
-- `ptrtoint` operand is globally unique per closure and no two initializers can
-- ever match.  Measured cost of the miss-only lookups (re-measured after S-1
-- routed capture-free user lambdas through this path too, not just eta-wrappers):
-- 902 `@mdk_cc_` globals in a full self-hosting `llvm_emit_modules_main` build of
-- this compiler, so up to ~406K miss comparisons (a linear scan against an
-- ever-growing list before each miss) — still a linear list scan per call, not
-- worth removing or restructuring, but the cache is dead weight, not working
-- dedup.
comments.code_after:
emitConstClosureCell : Emit -> String -> Int -> String
emitConstClosureCell e lamName arity =
  let codePtr = "ptrtoint (ptr @" ++ lamName ++ " to i64)"
  let initBody = "[2 x i64] [i64 \{intToString arity}, i64 \{codePtr}]"
  let key = constCellKey e initBody
  match lookupAssoc key !e.closConstCache
    Some gname => "ptrtoint (ptr @" ++ gname ++ " to i64)"
    None =>
      let gname = "mdk_cc" ++ mangleScoped e
      let _ = emitGlobal e "@\{gname} = internal constant \{initBody}"
      e.closConstCache := (key, gname) :: !e.closConstCache
      "ptrtoint (ptr @" ++ gname ++ " to i64)"

-- ── size-aware constructor choice (#2294) ───────────────────────────────────
-- Before this, `genUser` picked a constructor uniformly at random with no size
-- parameter.  For any ADT whose expected count of self-referential fields per
-- uniformly-chosen constructor exceeds 1 — `data T = Leaf | Node T T T`, mean
-- (0 + 3)/2 = 1.5 — that is a SUPERCRITICAL branching process: generation
-- diverges with positive probability on every draw, and the runner dies with
-- `E-STACK-OVERFLOW` rather than reporting anything.  (`End | One R | Two R R`
-- is mean 1.0 — critical: finite almost surely but with infinite expected
-- size, so it degrades rather than aborts.)
--
-- The fix biases the choice toward constructors that cannot recurse, more
-- strongly the deeper we already are, which drives the process subcritical
-- (mean < 1) and so back to finite expected size:
--
--   weight(v, depth) = if v can recurse then max 1 (recWeight0 - depth)
--                      else recWeight0
--
-- 🚨 At depth 0 — and at ANY depth for an ADT none of whose constructors can
-- reach the ADT ITSELF — every weight is `recWeight0`, i.e. the choice is
-- still UNIFORM.  That is the property that keeps this from silently narrowing
-- the value space every existing prop samples: such an ADT takes the
-- `allEqualInts` fast path below and draws the SAME `randIntRange 0 (n - 1)`
-- it always did, so its value stream is byte-identical.  Only a genuinely
-- recursive ADT, at depth ≥ 1, sees a different distribution — and it still
-- reaches every shape at the shallow depths, just not depth 1000.
--
-- ⚠️ "Can reach the ADT itself" is a REACHABILITY question over the type
-- graph, not a one-hop "mentions some user ADT" question.  Asking the latter
-- instead flags `F1` in
--
--   data Leaf = L0 | L1 ; data Fin = F0 | F1 Leaf
--
-- as recursive purely because `Leaf` is user-declared, even though `Leaf` can
-- never lead back to `Fin`.  Nested inside five non-recursive wrappers that
-- put `Fin` at depth 5, that drives P(F1) from the correct 0.5 down to 1/7 —
-- exactly the silent distribution narrowing this comment claims not to
-- happen.  `variantRecursive` therefore takes the OWNING ADT's name and asks
-- `adtReaches`, which walks the whole mention graph.
comments.code_after:
recWeight0 : Int
recWeight0 = 6
comments.note: header names #2294; "Before this" resolves to it

comments.comment:
-- A1 (poly-`Ord`-on-Float, string-free program): the num-only peer of emitValueCmpRef.
-- `==`/`/=` go through $mdk_value_eq_num (-> i31 Bool); ordering through $mdk_value_cmp_num
-- (-> i32 -1/0/1).  Both dispatch $float vs int (i31/$boxint) ONLY — no $str — so they
-- need no pre-scan-set type; gated by its own useValueCmpNum flag (S2/#2359 —
-- independent of the per-operator arith flags, since this branch never touches
-- $mdk_value_add/sub/mul/div/mod).
comments.code_after:
emitValueCmpNumRef : Prog ->
  List String ->
  Int ->
  String ->
  CExpr ->
  CExpr ->
  List String
emitValueCmpNumRef prog env d op l r =
  let lv = emitRefExpr prog env d l
  let rv = emitRefExpr prog env d r
  if op == "==" then
    lv ++ rv ++ ["call $mdk_value_eq_num"]
  else if op == "/=" then
    lv
      ++ rv
      ++ [
        "call $mdk_value_eq_num",
        "ref.cast (ref i31)",
        "i31.get_u",
        "i32.eqz",
        "ref.i31",
      ]
  else
comments.note: A1, S2/#2359 named

comments.comment:
-- #1110 ANSWER-PRESERVING, and it really does fire — the twin of `tupleSpine`'s
  -- rigid arm.  A real head is uppercase-initial OR one of the four reserved
  -- `__tupleN__` tags (`tupleCtorTyName`, `compiler/frontend/parser.mdk:2137-2141`,
  -- minted via `tyConBuiltin` at `:2131`), and `__tupleN__` is ALSO a legal rigid
  -- spelling: `identStartLower` (`compiler/frontend/lexer.mdk:1638`) admits a
  -- leading `_`, so `data Bad = Bad __tuple2__` binds a type PARAMETER and both
  -- rigid producers can mint `TRigid "__tuple2__"`.  Measured: without this arm
  -- `impl Q (,)` stops matching such a goal and a program that checked clean before
  -- the split becomes `No impl of Q for (,)` — a real answer change.
  --
  -- ⚠️ The pre-split answer this restores is a FORGERY: a rigid variable is not the
  -- builtin tuple head, and letting it match one is exactly the identity confusion
  -- DICT-SEMANTICS §8 I6.2(b) records as OWED-#1110.  Preserved deliberately —
  -- this PR is the carrier step; changing answers is the follow-on.
comments.code_after:
TRigid n2 => if n == n2 then MOk else MFail
  _ => MFail
matchStep (TyApp a b) m = match normalize m
  TApp ma mb => MKids [(a, ma), (b, mb)]
  _ => MFail
matchStep (TyTuple ts) m = match tupleSpine m
  Some ms => if listLen ts == listLen ms then MKids (zipL ts ms) else MFail
  _ => MFail
matchStep (TyFun a b) m = match normalize m
  TFun ma _ mb => MKids [(a, ma), (stripEff b, mb)]
  _ => MFail
matchStep (TyEffect _ _ t) m = MKids [(t, m)]
matchStep (TyConstrained _ t) m = MKids [(t, m)]
matchStep _ _ = MFail
comments.note: "this PR is the carrier step; changing answers is the follow-on"

comments.comment:
-- Core IR — STAGE2-DESIGN §2.1.  A serializable, backend-neutral intermediate
-- representation lowered from the elaborated (desugared + typed + dict-routed)
-- AST.  The Stage-2 design's load-bearing discipline (Axis 1, Condition 1) is
-- that this IR lives ABOVE any ISA: bytecode/LLVM are *lowerings* of it, never
-- the IR itself, so the lexical-addressing, decision-tree-match and dict-routing
-- work transfers to whichever backend consumes it.
--
-- What makes this a Core IR rather than a copy of `ast.mdk`'s `Expr`:
--   • DESUGARED — only the core node set survives (sugar already lowered by
--     desugar.mdk: sections, comprehensions, do/blocks, guards→if/fallthrough).
--   • PRIMITIVE — surface operators that are really sugar are lowered away here:
--     `&&`/`||`→`CIf` (short-circuit preserved), `|>`→`CApp`, `>>`/`<<`→`CLam`.
--     Only the genuinely-primitive binops survive as `CBinPrim` (arith, compare,
--     `::`, `++`).
--   • LEXICALLY ADDRESSED — every variable carries its resolved `Addr` (the
--     `(frame,slot)` from STAGE2-DESIGN §2.0).  Slice-1 carries it structurally;
--     the slot-indexing consume-half (eval over array frames) is 2.0's parked
--     supervised rework, so today's `ceval` still resolves by name — exactly the
--     status of the `EVarAt` EMIT half in `ast.mdk`.
--   • DICTS EXPLICIT — typeclass dispatch is the structural `CMethod`/`CDict`
--     carrying the typechecker's resolved `Route`s (immutable here — the AST's
--     `Ref Route` mutable cell is read out at lowering time).  These are the
--     "dictionaries already explicit" the design names as the foundation both
--     backends share.  (Emitted/evaluated from slice 5 on; present now so the IR
--     type is complete.)
--   • EFFECTS FULLY ERASED — the frozen-IR contract for effect-polymorphism
--     (STAGE2-DESIGN §2.3).  Effects are TYPE-level only: they live inside `Ty`
--     (`TyEffect`, `ast.mdk`) and the typechecker's `EffRow`/`Effvar` arrows
--     (`typecheck.mdk`), never as standalone expression nodes, and the language
--     has NO runtime effect construct (no perform/handle/resume — Phase 146 is a
--     typecheck-time discipline: open-row inference, propagation, escape,
--     laundering).  So effects erase WITH types at lowering
--     (`lower (EAnnot e _) = lower e` in core_ir_lower.mdk) and the runtime has
--     nothing to witness.  Representation after erasure, stated as a freeze:
--     an effect-polymorphic function is represented IDENTICALLY to a monomorphic
--     one — no effect node, no effect parameter, no effect-directed dispatch.
--     This is the exact OPPOSITE of typeclass polymorphism: a `=>` constraint
--     carries a runtime witness (the `CMethod`/`CDict` dict above); a `<e>`
--     effect row carries NONE.  Dispatch is type-head directed, not effect
--     directed, so erasure cannot perturb a `Route`.  (Verified by equivalence:
--     a combinator instantiated at an effectful row and at the pure row evaluates
--     identically across tree-walker / Core IR / bytecode VM — fixture
--     `test/eval_fixtures/effect_poly.mdk`; the Core IR dump carries 0 effect
--     tokens.)
--
-- Validation (the net-new-IR oracle problem, §2.1): there is no OCaml reference
-- for Core IR.  It is validated by EQUIVALENCE — lower the elaborated AST to Core
-- IR, evaluate the IR (core_ir_eval.mdk), and diff stdout/pp_value against the
-- AST tree-walker over the whole fixture corpus.  Core IR is correct iff
-- evaluating it matches evaluating the AST.
comments.code_after: import frontend.ast.{Lit, Pat, Addr, Route}
comments.note: design-doc citations only

  -- `ieSnapAt` routes through `ieCandidacyVisibleAt`, which is `True`, so this binding is

  -- A-3's C4/I2 claim is cashed: every obligation check on the multi-module path knows the

  -- order`, IS GONE FROM THE TREE (derive: `ls test/must_fail_fixtures | grep 1072`) — see

  --

  -- kept so the call site does not move and so re-scoping candidacy later is a
  -- one-line change; do not "simplify" it away, and do not read its presence as

comments.comment:
-- #1559 A-3.7: DO TWO IMPL OCCURRENCES NAME THE SAME INTERFACE?
--
-- 🚨 `sameTyConHead`, NEVER `ifaceIdMatches`, AND THE TWO ARE EXACT INVERSES.  This
-- is the whole substance of the bite, so the derivation is here rather than in a
-- ledger:
--   * `sameTyConHead n1 o1 n2 o2 = n1 == n2 && not (tyConIdsConflict o1 o2)`
--     (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — name equality, and an ABSENT origin makes NO CLAIM, so
--     it matches anything.
--   * `ifaceIdMatches a b = a /= "" && a == b` (`frontend/ast.mdk`) — absence NEVER
--     matches, not even itself.
-- `recordCandIsType`'s header states which to use when, and the rule is about the
-- QUESTION being asked, not about the table: `sameTyConHead` belongs where a false
-- REJECT would refuse a valid program (an ACCEPTANCE question); `ifaceIdMatches`
-- belongs where a false HIT is silent wrongness (a LOOKUP).
--
-- Coherence is an ACCEPTANCE question — it decides whether to reject a program — so
-- `sameTyConHead` is correct, and it is also the FAIL-LOUD direction here: an impl
-- whose `implOrigin` is still `OriginUnresolved` compares by name exactly as it did
-- before this unit, so no live rejection can silently vanish.  `ifaceIdMatches` in
-- this position would turn every unstamped-origin conflict into a SILENT ACCEPT,
-- which is a severity INCREASE and one no fixture in the tree would catch.
--
-- ⚠️ NOT a re-keying of the HEAD half.  Coherence's head comparison already routes
-- through `sameTyConHead` (`cohGoR`'s `TCon` arm, A-2.10) and is untouched, so the
-- #1317 T1 rule and closed S0 #1277 are not in scope for this unit.
comments.code_after:
cohSameIface : IfaceRef -> IfaceRef -> Bool
cohSameIface a b = sameTyConHead a.irName a.irOrigin b.irName b.irOrigin
comments.note: "before this unit" but #1559 A-3.7 heads the block

comments.comment:
-- #822 (graded interfaces): an instance head must have the KIND the interface's
-- corresponding type parameter has.  A graded interface binds the whole row-indexed
-- FAMILY — `impl GThenable Async`, never a fixed row like `impl GThenable (Async e)`
-- (EFFECTS-SEMANTICS §6, DICT-SEMANTICS §3) — so the head's REMAINING parameter
-- kinds (its declared kinds minus the ones the head already applied) must equal the
-- interface slot's kinds.
--
-- This is a soundness guard, not polish.  A kind-mismatched head elaborates the
-- method type's KRow slot to a `TEff` row while the constructor's own scheme has a
-- plain tyvar in that position, and `unify` binds a tyvar to a TEff without
-- complaint: the impl would be ACCEPTED and its grade would mean nothing — every
-- index a caller reads off the result would be a fabrication.
--
-- Only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are JUDGED — the `anyKRow want`
-- guard below is what does that, not the table: every slot of every interface is
-- recorded (it always was, and `ceRowParamKinds` keeps doing so), and an all-`KType`
-- row falls into the same `_ => ()` arm an outright miss does.  ⚠️ This paragraph
-- read *"only interfaces that actually HAVE a graded slot are inspected
-- (ifaceParamKindsRef records nothing else)"* until #1557 A-3.5c, and the
-- parenthetical was false of the retired table too.  Runs on BOTH whole-program
-- paths: its one call site is in checkBodyImpl, shared by Flat and Module,
-- immediately after `dataEnv` has populated the head-constructor kind table.
--
-- 🚨 #1557 A-3.5c: IT STILL ITERATES `prog`, AND THAT IS THE UNIT'S DEFINING
-- CONDITION, not an implementation detail.  The owner ruling that split A-3.5c
-- out of the A-3b lane (issue #1557, 2026-08-12) is CONDITIONAL: this check
-- qualifies as CE-only *"only if the graded impl-head kind check keeps
-- iterating `prog` rather than `IE.ieRows`"*.  The impl HEADS come from the
-- decl list; only the interface's declared slot kinds come from stage K's `CE`.
-- Whoever re-points this walk at `IE.ieRows` has re-classified the unit as A-3b
-- by construction — that is a routing decision, not a refactor.
comments.code_after:
checkGradedImplHeads : ClassEnv -> Int -> List Decl -> Unit
checkGradedImplHeads _ _ [] = ()
checkGradedImplHeads ce cur (d :: rest) =
  let _ = checkGradedImplHeadDecl ce cur d
  checkGradedImplHeads ce cur rest
comments.note: #822 / #1557 A-3.5c named; dated owner ruling

comments.comment:
-- extern declarations become top-level schemes (like interface methods)
--
-- 🚨 #1280: THE STAMPING WALK IS PART OF THIS FUNCTION, NOT OF ITS CALLERS, AND
-- THAT IS THE FIX.  Every other tree that reaches typecheck has already been
-- through `stampTyOrigins` at a driver (`stampGraphTyOrigins` on the module arm,
-- `stampFlatTyOrigins` inside `checkProgramSeededSplit` on the flat one).
-- `runtimeDecls` was the one tree that reached a `Scheme` without ever entering
-- that walk on EITHER arm, so every `Mono` `fromAstTypeE` built out of an extern's
-- declared type carried `OriginUnresolved` — the SUPPLY half of the dispatch-key
-- blocker recorded at `dispHeadTab`, and the absent head #1279 bridges two
-- distinct identities through.
--
-- The scope is a parameter and not a `List Decl` prelude on purpose: two
-- `List Decl` arguments are positionally interchangeable and `stampTyHead`'s
-- immunity rule makes a wrong first stamp PERMANENT (`stampFlatTyOrigins`'
-- comment in `frontend/resolve.mdk` records that hazard costing a defect once
-- already).  Build it with `externTyOriginScope`, which owns the derivation of
-- WHY one scope is right for this population on both arms.
--
-- ⚠️ `externTyOriginScope []` at a call site is not a shrug: it is the same
-- "prelude boundary unknown" answer `checkProgramSeededSplit` gives when its
-- `coreProg0` is `[]` — those callers have already FLATTENED the prelude into the
-- program they check, so the prelude's own `Option`/`Ordering`/`Result`
-- declarations are unstamped on that path too and the two sides stay symmetric.
-- The builtin layer is still supplied there, so it is strictly more identity than
-- before, never a claim the driver cannot justify.
--
-- 🚨 FILTER BEFORE STAMPING, AND THAT ORDER IS PERFORMANCE, NOT STYLE.  The first
-- cut here was `externSchemesGo (stampTyOrigins scope decls)`, which is a no-op
-- difference for `runtimeDecls` (every element IS a `DExtern`) and wrong-shaped at
-- the `checkBodyImpl` call site, where `decls` is the WHOLE MODULE.  Read the
-- chain rather than take this on trust: `stampTyOrigins` is `map
-- (stampDeclTyOrigins scope)`, and `stampDeclTyOrigins` is `mapOriginsInDecl`,
-- i.e. a full `mapTyInDecl` REBUILD of the decl — so that shape reconstructs every
-- declaration in the program and then discards all but the externs, in a stage
-- `compiler/AGENTS.md` calls GC-bound.  Filtering first makes the walk
-- proportional to the externs, which is all this function reads.
--

-- Phase / GAP-2 phase-a: the tyvar ids that some ARG-position method occurrence
-- discriminates on (the receiver monos queued in pendingArgStamps).  A where-helper
-- whose own type shares one of these is *method-constrained by the enclosing fn's
-- dispatch* — its receiver var unifies (at the helper's call site) with the
-- enclosing fn's constraint var that activeDictVars maps to a dict param.  We must
-- NOT generalize over such a var, or the helper instantiates a fresh (id /= the
-- enclosing constraint var) so resolveArgStamp can't see the in-scope dict → the
-- in-body method route degrades to RNone → arg-tag → native panic on a primitive
-- receiver.  Keeping it monomorphic links the ids (normalize collapses them) so the
-- existing resolveArgStamp routes RDict and dict_pass threads the enclosing dict in.
-- Sound: an UNconstrained helper var (e.g. `pair x = (x,x)`) never appears in a
-- method-usage mono, so it still generalizes; only dispatch-constrained vars (which
-- compiler cannot dict-pass per-where-helper anyway) are pinned, matching their
-- single enclosing-typed use.
--
-- #866 pairs each such id with the INTERFACE of the method that discriminates on it, so
-- a binding pinned by the METHOD channel gets the same explanatory diagnostic as one
-- pinned by the dict channel.  The interface is NOTE-ONLY: an entry whose method has no
-- registered interface contributes `""` (see argStampPairs) and so silently contributes
-- no note, falling back to the plain mismatch, rather than dropping out of the pin and
-- changing what typechecks.
--
-- #2445 S-1: this used to have an id-only twin, `methodConstrainedIds`, which
-- `localPinIds` called directly.  `localPinIds` is now `map fst` of `localPinPairs` — the
-- equality both functions' comments already asserted, made structural so the unpin hatch
-- has ONE read site — which left the twin (and its `argStampMono` accessor) with no
-- caller, so they are gone.  Nothing about the CHANNEL changed: this is the same
-- `flatMap` over the same `pendingArgStamps`, in the same order, and `map fst` of it is
-- byte-for-byte what the twin returned.
comments.code_after:
methodConstrainedPairs : Unit -> List (Int, String)
methodConstrainedPairs _ =
  flatMap argStampPairs (siteGoals GKArgStamp (currentModuleMarks ()).mGoals)
comments.note: GAP-2 phase-a, #866, #2445 S-1 named

      -- non-head quantified variables — type AND effect — belong to the CALLER
      -- (every use site re-instantiates them freshly), so the body must be checked
      -- at full generality.  [extraMap]/[effMap] were fresh flexible vars for the
      -- unify above; verifying they SURVIVED unification as distinct unbound
      -- variables (types) / atom-free rows with distinct tails (effects) is

      -- post-unify inspection (the same discipline as checkAnnotTooGeneral's C3).

      -- instantiates b := String, evaluation crashes) or to an effect-bearing
      -- arrow, alone or nested in a tuple/data arg (caller pins b to the pure
      -- arrow: a certified-pure value performs IO — the #814 laundering vein the
      -- per-arrow #803 walk above is structurally blind to).  Runs BEFORE
      -- defaultBodyLocalNum so a body-local Num default can never mask a pin.
      -- [addedObls] (this body's obligation window, also fed to defaultBodyLocalNum
      -- below) carries the CONSTRAINT axis: a body whose pin is a *constrained
      -- var* rather than a constructed type (`mk d = 42` pins b to a Num-obligated

      -- resolves to the module the unit imports it from, not the universe's load-order
      -- winner.  Reads the persistent universe DECLS (not the Module `accData` field —
      -- that is dead `[]` on the elaborate/emit path, #154 PR-C), so the overlay fires
      -- on the run/build gate too, not just `check`.

      --     universe  <  imported-ctor overlay  <  this module's OWN `prog0`.
      -- The overlay registers AFTER the universe (that is #674's requirement — it must
      -- win the `omInsert` tie-break over the load-order winner) and BEFORE `prog0`
      -- (this module's own declarations outrank anything it imports — ordinary
      -- shadowing, and the SHADOW spec's S1 per-module scoping).

      -- ⚠️ Registering the overlay LAST, over `prog0`, is a REGRESSION and shipped as
      -- one: an imported decl's constructors then beat locally-declared ones, so
      -- `import json.{Json, JNull}` + a local `data Tok = JString String` was rejected
      -- `Type mismatch: Json vs Tok` — clobbered by a SIBLING constructor of `Json`
      -- that the program never imported.  It reaches the stdlib and it is not narrow:
      -- every selective constructor-naming import carries it.  Pinned by
      -- `test/engine_fixtures/ctor_scope_local_ctor_beats_stdlib_import.mdk` (the
      -- stdlib `json` shape, on all three engines) and
      -- `test/llvm_fixtures_modules/ctor_scope_local_decl_wins/` (`{Ext, Other}` plus
      -- a local decl, prelude-free).
      --
      -- 🚨 THE SET OF ORDER-OBSERVABLE STRUCTURES — enumerate it, because #674's root
      -- cause was exactly two of them disagreeing, and a FUTURE edit re-creates that by
      -- moving ONE.  This note used to name a PAIR ("both structures agree"), and the
      -- pair it named was the one that cannot disagree — while omitting the one that can.
      --
      -- Registration order here is  universe < overlay < prog0.  Under it:
      --   * the `TcEnv` ctor scheme map (`addCtor` → `omInsert`, BARE ctor name) —
      --     LAST-write-wins → prog0.  BARE-keyed, so two modules genuinely collide here;
      --     this is #1259's table and the one the overlay exists for.
      --   * `recordByNameRef` (`registerRecordInfoKeyed` → `omInsert`, BARE ctor name) —
      --     LAST-write-wins → prog0.  #1256's table, same keying, same hazard.
      --   * `dataParamKindsRef` (`recordParamKinds`, a consed list read FIRST-match) —
      --     prepend order [prog0, overlay, universe] → prog0.  ⚠️ This one is
      --     IDENTITY-keyed since A-2.3 (`tyTabKey o name`), so two modules' same-named
      --     types get DIFFERENT keys and registration order cannot decide between them
      --     at all.  It is order-observable only for a decl registered twice, where it
      --     agrees.  It is NOT evidence about the bare-keyed tables above.
      --   * the exhaust ctor ORACLE — and it is built at a DIFFERENT CALL SITE
      --     (`checkModuleFullDiags`: `seedCheckRun (prog ++ importedCtorTypeDeclsFirstWins prog …
      --     ++ accData)`), from a LIST, with `oracleMap` = `omFromPairs (reverseL …)`,

      --     opposite mechanism, and reached through none of the code on this line.
      --     THIS is the one a future edit can silently flip, so check it too.
      -- All four land on prog0 > overlay > universe.  Getting any two to disagree is
      -- #674's root cause.

      -- than a fifth registration — `applyCtorScopeOverrides` re-points the (normally
      -- empty) set of COLLIDED constructor names at the declaration THIS module's import

-- ── Backing store ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Wraps the EXISTING `OrdMap` (`support/ordmap.mdk`, itself a transparent
-- alias for stdlib `Map String a`) rather than reaching for stdlib `map`/
-- `hash_map` directly. `support/ordmap.mdk` is already imported by
-- `types/typecheck.mdk`, so this pays NOTHING extra: `Map`'s Eq/Ord/Debug/
-- Display/Mappable/Monoid instance surface is already forced into the
-- binary. Importing a stdlib module that defines a brand NEW type (e.g.
-- `map` cold, or `hash_map`) from a module that does not already transitively
-- pull it in is the anti-pattern `AGENTS.md` measures at +34 KB / +4.8%
-- self-compile (DCE keeps a `DImpl`/`DInterface` whole once it is
-- reachable at all) — this module avoids that by riding the SAME `OrdMap`
-- everything else already rides. `map.{entries}` below is likewise
-- already-forced surface (`entries` operates on the already-forced `Map`
-- type), so it adds no new retained instance surface.
--
-- ── `identKey`: the ONE renderer, collision-free by construction ───────────
-- Every component (namespace tag, origin tag, origin module-or-empty, name)
-- is rendered through `lenKey` (`support/util.mdk`) — a length-prefixed
-- ("netstring") encoding: `lenKey s = "\{intToString (stringLength s)}:\{s}"`.
-- This is the SAME collision-free composite-key technique
-- `support/util.mdk`'s own callers already rely on (see its `lenKey`
-- doc-comment). Concatenating length-prefixed fields cannot let one field's
-- content bleed into the next boundary REGARDLESS of what characters the
-- fields contain — no separator character to reserve, so there is no
-- "adversarial name contains the separator" case to guard against (the
-- doctests below instead demonstrate the sharper adversarial case: two
-- DIFFERENT `(origin module, name)` pairs that share a character at their
-- boundary, e.g. `("ab", "c")` vs. `("a", "bc")`, which a naive `++`
-- concatenation WOULD collide on and `lenKey`-prefixing does not).
--
-- Each `identKey` is a group of EXACTLY FOUR netstrings, and a netstring
-- stream is uniquely decodable (the length prefix is all digits, so the
-- first `:` is always the delimiter). Both facts are load-bearing for the
-- composite keys below.
--
-- `identKey`'s output is OPAQUE TO CONSUMERS: no code outside this module may
-- parse it back, and this module's own non-test code does not either.
-- `regEntries` therefore does not reconstruct an `Ident` from the rendered
-- key — it keeps the original `RegKey` alongside its value in the backing map
-- instead, so recovering identities never depends on the key being decodable.
--
-- ⚠️ THIS MODULE'S TESTS ARE A STATED EXCEPTION, AND DELETING THEM WOULD BE A
-- REGRESSION, NOT A CLEANUP. Several assertions in
-- `compiler/types/registry_test.mdk` read the key's BYTES on purpose (`identKey
-- identTypeFooM == "4:type6:module1:m3:Foo"` and the three `startsWith "1:…"`
-- count-prefix lines). They are not consumers violating the contract; they are
-- the only witnesses to two invariants that no property-level test can see —
-- that the origin TAG is present, and that the ident-COUNT prefix is present.
-- Both are documented below as defense in depth precisely because the module
-- still behaves correctly without them TODAY, so a reviewer who reads only
-- this paragraph, concludes the byte-reading tests violate the contract, and
-- deletes them removes the one thing keeping injectivity independent of
-- `nsTag`'s alphabet. The contract is: opaque to CONSUMERS, transparent to the
-- tests that pin the encoding.
--
-- ── Where the tests are ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The doctests kept in this file ILLUSTRATE a return value to a reader. The
-- boolean assertions about the same machinery — the ones standing in for unit
-- tests — live in the sibling `compiler/types/registry_test.mdk`, which
-- redeclares the fixtures it needs rather than importing them, so no doctest
-- fixture reaches this module's public surface. Three of those boolean
-- assertions could not move: the ones naming `OriginUnresolved`, because
-- `test/typecheck_compiler_source.sh`'s #1110 producer ratchet pins the set of
-- tracked files carrying a live mention of that sentinel.
--
-- ── What the target tables need: COMPOSITE keys (`RegKey`) — see
-- `compiler/TYPECHECK-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md` §11 for the RegKey design
-- record: the five target tables and their composite-key shapes (§11.1),
-- `regInsert`'s LAST-WRITE-WINS conflict handling (§11.2), and why a
-- re-keying conversion is not automatically behavior-preserving (§11.3).
--
-- ⚠️ `IdentOrigin` is imported WITHOUT `(..)` — its constructors are private
-- to `frontend/ast.mdk` so that `IdentModule ""` is unrepresentable (see the
-- type's doc-comment there).  `identOriginFold` is the eliminator, and
-- `mkIdent`/`identOriginBuiltin` are the only mints.

  Ns(..),
  Ident(..),
  IdentOrigin,
  TyConOrigin(..),

-- ── the loader's error channel (issue #100) ─────────────────────────────────
--
-- A load failure is DATA, not a panic.  `LoadMsg` carries the pre-existing
-- free-text failures verbatim (unknown module / cyclic dependency / unreadable
-- file), so every caller that only wants a string is unaffected via
-- `loadErrorMessage`.  `LoadParseFailed path src err` is the structured half: a
-- parse or lex error inside a MODULE of the graph, carrying the owning module's
-- FILE PATH and the exact SOURCE that was parsed, plus the located `ParseError`.
--
-- Both extra fields are load-bearing.  The path is the whole point: before this,
-- the parser panicked and the failure lost the module it belonged to, so the
-- driver could only ever attribute it to the ENTRY file.  The source must travel
-- WITH the error rather than be re-read by the caller, because under the LSP's
-- unsaved-buffer `read` override the on-disk bytes are NOT what was parsed —
-- re-reading would render the caret against stale text.
comments.note: #100 named

comments.comment:
-- N5 (inherited, slice 1): entry ABSENCE means "no argument vector was recorded for this
-- callee at all", and every reader turns it into `(slot, [])` — the historical scalar
-- per-tyvar goal, byte for byte.  A row of all-empty vectors reads identically at every
-- reader, same-module and cross-module alike, so writing one would only ADD a
-- `funConstraintArgsRef` / `crossModuleFunConstraintArgsQualRef` row that says nothing.
-- Recover nothing ⇒ write nothing, exactly as before this slice.
-- #23: the iface name for an inferred constraint var.  `ifaceForConstraintId` only
-- recovers it from a pendingImplObligation whose `occ` is a BARE `TVar id`; a
-- constraint induced by a `fromInt`/method site records a COMPOUND occ (the whole
-- method type), so it returns "" — leaving the call site's dict route unkeyed
-- (`routeUndeterminedTop ""` → RNone → a NULL Num dict word → build SIGTRAP, while
-- `medaka run` is correct).  Two FALLBACKS recover the name when ifaceForConstraintId
-- returns "" (so existing non-"" routes stay byte-identical):
--   (1) `schemeObligationsRef` pairs each scheme var with its iface via
--       `dispatchMonosOf` (robust to compound occs); covers a fn whose own body has
--       the literal/method site (`app2 f = f 2 3`).
--   (2) a constraint FORWARDED from a constrained callee (`useApp g = app2 g`) never
--       lands in pendingImplObligations/schemeObligations — its iface lives in the
--       `pendingDictApps` entry the callee's inferDictAtFound recorded (slot-parallel
--       monos/ifaces).  Scan it for the var at a slot whose iface is now known.
-- Both run AFTER the callee's own constraints are registered (topological SCC order),
-- so the forwarded callee's ifaces are populated.
-- U1b (#1482): returns an `IfaceRef`, since `funConstraintIfacesRef` now stores one.
-- Fallbacks (1) and (2) carry a real occurrence identity — `implObls` and
-- `schemeObligationsRef` both hold one.  Fallback (3) CANNOT and does not pretend to:
-- a `GKDictApp` goal stores a route WORD (see `resolveDictApps` / `dispHeadTab`), so
-- its recovery is bare by construction.  The scan is over the CURRENT module's goals
-- only: an earlier module's application of the same scheme var id would be a stale
-- read under the graph-wide counter.  `ifaceRefNone` is the "no interface here" sentinel,
-- which is a different fact from "identity unrecoverable".
comments.code_after:
ifaceForInferredId : String -> Int -> IfaceRef
ifaceForInferredId m id =
  let direct = ifaceForConstraintId id
  if direct.irName /= "" then
    direct
  else match lookupSchemeIface m id perRun.value.schemeObligationsRef.value
    Some ir => ir
    None =>
      match ifaceFromDictApps id (dictAppsSince (currentModuleMarks ()).mGoals)
        "" => ifaceRefNone
        n => ifaceRefBare n

comments.comment:
-- ── the stdlib reference index ────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A name → DECLARED-SIGNATURE map for every exported stdlib binding, built by
-- PARSING `<MEDAKA_ROOT>/stdlib/*.mdk` and reading each exported `DTypeSig`.
-- It is the reference a style rule consults instead of a hand-curated name
-- list: the stdlib is the source of truth, so the index cannot drift from it.
--
-- Signatures come from the SOURCE, never from the typechecker's `ppScheme`:
-- lint runs on the RAW pre-desugar AST with no type environment at all (there
-- is no inferred scheme to read), and what a hand-rolled user binding has to be
-- compared against is what the stdlib author WROTE.
--
-- 🚨 A STDLIB NAME IS NOT UNIQUE, so the index maps a name to a LIST of
-- (module, type), never to one type.  Measured on this tree: 55 of the 396
-- exported names are declared in more than one stdlib module, and `reverse` is
-- declared in THREE — `array.reverse : Array a -> Array a`,
-- `list.reverse : List a -> List a`, `string.reverse : String -> String`.
-- A flat `HashMap String Ty` silently keeps whichever file `listDir` yielded
-- last: `reverse` then reads back as `String -> String`, and every List-shaped
-- question about it gets a String-shaped answer with no error anywhere.  That
-- is the bare-name-keyed-table failure mode AGENTS.md's [T-GLOBAL-TABLE] names,
-- and it is invisible to any check that only asks whether a name is PRESENT —
-- this index was written flat first and the flat version passed exactly that
-- test while answering `reverse` wrong.  Consumers must therefore say WHICH
-- module they mean (`stdlibSigIn`) or handle every candidate
-- (`stdlibEntriesOf`); there is deliberately no "the signature of X" accessor,
-- because for 55 names there is no such thing.  `stdlibAmbiguousNames` is that
-- set, derived — never a list written down here.
--
-- ⚠️ `Rule.check` is PURE and reading the stdlib needs `<IO>`, so the index is
-- never built inside a rule.  Each IO entry point builds it ONCE and passes it
-- down through `lintProgram` as `check`'s first argument.
--
-- DEGRADATION.  Every failure mode — `MEDAKA_ROOT` unset and the exe-relative
-- fallback wrong, no `stdlib/` directory, an unreadable or unparseable member —
-- yields an EMPTY index (or one missing that member), never a crash and never a
-- wrong entry.  Same self-disabling shape `lintCacheCtx` uses for
-- `crossFileCacheSound` (`driver/medaka_cli.mdk`): a degraded run costs findings
-- it could have made, never findings it should not have made.
--
-- POSITIONAL, not a named-field record, and read ONLY through the helpers
-- below — the same native field-scanner reason `Rule` documents.
comments.code_after:
public export data StdlibIndex =
  | StdlibIndex (HashMap String (List (String, Ty)))
comments.note: "Measured on this tree" is measurement provenance, not an in-flight change

comments.comment:
-- inferLetGroup's ELetGroup is DIFFERENT: it is the SAME node `where` clauses
-- desugar to (parser.mdk whereEol/whereTail/guard-arm-where — verified: no
-- `rec` keyword involved, no AST field distinguishing the two), and a `where`
-- group routinely bundles plain, NON-recursive value helpers alongside real
-- functions (e.g. stdlib/list.mdk's `split`: `where sepLen = length sep; go
-- ys = …` — sepLen never mentions itself or any sibling). Applying
-- checkRecBindNonFunction's blunt "not a lambda ⇒ reject" rule here false-
-- positived on exactly that (confirmed against the tree before landing this).
--
-- So this check is narrower and more precise instead of broader: a zero-param,
-- non-lambda clause is illegal only if its RHS EAGERLY (i.e. not deferred
-- behind a nested lambda) mentions itself or a NOT-YET-INSTALLED sibling — the
-- actual hazard (evalLetGroup pre-binds every member's cell to Ref VUnit and
-- installs each member's value in SOURCE ORDER, so an eager reference to a
-- cell installed BEFORE this one is already set — safe — while a reference to
-- itself or a cell installed AFTER this one reads stale VUnit — unsafe).
--
-- Concretely: for the clause at index i, only a self-or-FORWARD reference
-- (index >= i) is illegal; a BACKWARD reference (index < i) is the ordinary,
-- safe `where`-clause shape (`f x = b where a = x + 1; b = a + 100` — `b`
-- referencing the earlier `a` is fine, `a` referencing the later `b` would not
-- be). checkLetGroupBindsGo threads exactly that suffix: at each step the
-- current binding's own name is prepended to the REST of the list (every
-- sibling that installs after it), so "names" passed down is always "self +
-- forward", never "self + every sibling" — an earlier false-positive this
-- fixed (confirmed against the tree: it rejected working `where`-bound values
-- that only referenced an EARLIER sibling).
comments.code_after:
checkLetGroupBindsLocated : List LetBind -> Unit
checkLetGroupBindsLocated = checkLetGroupBindsGo
comments.note: "confirmed against the tree before landing this" -- landing WHAT is unrecoverable

-- ── Cross-cutting identity substrate (#1111 A-2.0) ─────────────────────────
-- `Ns` + `Ident` generalize `TyConOrigin` from "which module declared this
-- TYPE head" to "which module declared this declaration, IN WHICH
-- NAMESPACE" — the substrate the Stage A-2 table-conversion units (each its
-- own PR) re-key their `universe*`/method/record/kind tables onto.  The
-- `Registry`/`MultiRegistry`/`SetRegistry` combinators built on top of
-- `Ident` live in `compiler/types/registry.mdk`: they need
-- `support/ordmap.mdk`, a dependency this file has no other reason to gain.
-- `Ns`/`IdentOrigin`/`Ident` are plain data with no such dependency, so they
-- sit beside the `TyConOrigin` they are derived from.
--
-- ── Gate cost of that split — MEASURED 2026-08-03 ──────────────────────────
-- ⚠️ DERIVE, do not trust these three numbers.  One command per path:
--   PREFLIGHT_DRY=1 PREFLIGHT_CHANGED_FILE=<file naming ONE path> sh test/preflight.sh
-- As measured on this tree: `compiler/frontend/ast.mdk` selects **16** gates;
-- `compiler/types/registry.mdk` selects **25** — the byte-identical set that
-- `compiler/types/typecheck.mdk` selects, so the new module costs a later
-- A-2 unit NOTHING (each such unit edits `typecheck.mdk` anyway).
-- `compiler/support/util.mdk` selects **103** (`test/preflight.sh`'s
-- `mark_full` blast-radius arm), which is the actual reason the combinators
-- are not in `compiler/support/`.
-- 🚨 An earlier draft of this comment called `ast.mdk` a "~26-gate import
-- surface" and `types/registry.mdk` "narrower".  Both numbers were invented
-- and the COMPARISON WAS INVERTED — `ast.mdk` is the narrower of the two
-- (16 < 25).  The split is therefore justified by the `support/` figure
-- above and by the dependency direction, NOT by ast-vs-registry gate counts.
--
-- SIX namespaces, matching the six declaration kinds #1070 catalogs as
-- distinct collision surfaces: a type name, an interface name, an interface
-- method name, a data/newtype constructor name, a record field name, and an
-- ordinary top-level value name are six independent spellings-may-collide
-- domains.  MEASURED 2026-08-03, exit 0: `data Cfg = MkCfg { size : Int }`
-- plus `interface Sizeable a where size : a -> Int` in one file checks
-- clean — `size` names two different declarations, in the FIELD and METHOD
-- namespaces, without colliding as declarations.  ONE `Ns`-tagged `Ident`

-- comparator (`deriving (Eq, Ord, Debug)` below — ONE derivation, not six),

-- one place a namespace tag can be forgotten.

-- IFACE namespaces share ONE `OrdMap TyConOrigin` separated by an

-- CONSTRAINT VAR'S ID — the same rule #1177 established for the SIGNATURE `=>` channel,
-- on the channel #1177 did not reach.  `registerReqSlots` opens one dict slot per
-- `requires` ENTRY but keys `activeDictVars` on the tyvar ids INSIDE the entry, so
-- `impl Sh (Box a) requires Ix a Char, Dbg2 a` registers `a`'s id TWICE — once per slot.
-- `firstDictForEncl` then scans a cons-list whose head is the LAST registration, so
-- EVERY method use in the body read the LAST slot: `ix x 'z'` read the `Dbg2` dict, its
-- route degraded, and first-declared-`impl Ix` won.  MEASURED on the typed Core IR dump
-- at this slice's base — `sh`'s body lowered to `CMethod "ix" (RDict "$dict_sh_1")` and
-- `CMethod "dbg2" (RDict "$dict_sh_1")`, with `$dict_sh_0` bound and never read — which
-- is why moving the `Ix` entry to the END of the `requires` list (a meaning-preserving
-- edit) moved the answer from 116 to the correct 227.

-- ⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE `argReqRoute`/`EKNestedTop` GOAL-VECTOR SEAM, AND THAT SEAM IS NOT
-- BROKEN.  The routes handed to the call site are already correct at every position
-- (`(RKey "Ix|Int Char|") (RKey "Int")`, in `requires` order); the loss is entirely on
-- the CONSUMPTION side, in which slot the impl BODY reads.  A fix aimed at the routing
-- ladder would have moved nothing.
--
-- A complete request uses one exact pass.  A miss is terminal at
-- `activeDictVarOfEncl`; only an explicit no-predicate route may consult scalar state.
--
-- #2547 unit 3: the scan is `firstPredForEnclAt` — the id-gated given lookup — not a
-- private `implReqPick`.  The two were term-for-term the same test over the same pair in
-- opposite tuple orders; one given environment leaves one of them.

implReqDictVarOf : Option PredicateRequest ->
  Mono ->
  String ->
  ScopeId ->
  Option AssumAnswer
implReqDictVarOf None _ _ _ = None
implReqDictVarOf (Some request) m encl useScope
  | encl == "" = None
  | otherwise = match normalize m
    TVar cell =>
      firstPredForEnclAt
        GSImplRequires
        (tyvarId cell)
        request
        useScope
        (givensForScope useScope)
    TApp a _ => implReqDictVarOf (Some request) a encl useScope
    _ => None

-- `resolve.mdk`'s consumer rule — *"NO predicate may compare two

-- #54: the SECOND disjunct of definerShadowArgHead — the IMPORTER-on-emit signal, kept
-- separate because it carries a DIFFERENT gate from the definer one.  The mark pass seeds
-- an importer shadow's route with the provider's mangled standalone symbol, so a non-empty
-- route symbol says "this is a shadow" cross-module, where definerShadowNamesRef (keyed on
-- module-local funDefs) cannot.  It stays scoped to singleTyparamIfaceMethod because what
-- it feeds is Fork 1's per-receiver rule; the definer disjunct (isDefinerShadow) does not,
-- because the S2 inversion never queries the impl universe.  On the un-mangled run/check
-- path the route is RNone (sym ""), so this is inert there.
--
-- L4: this predicate now names its two conjuncts separately instead of conflating them in
-- one `routeLocalSym … /= ""` test.  `driverState.value.mangledFunDefsPresentRef.value`
-- (L3) is the GRAPH-level fact "this compile's decls carry mangled funDefs at all";
-- `occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym tagRef` is the mark pass's own PER-OCCURRENCE verdict
-- for THIS route.  The new graph-level conjunct is ADDED, not substituted for the
-- occurrence test — F7 (this file) forbids replacing the per-occurrence route test with a
-- graph-wide one: doing so would fire for occurrences the mark pass never marked, and
-- would pin genuine method-values, breaking dispatch.
--
-- 🚨 RUN-XMOD-045 CORRECTION (post-landing, slice-breaker finding) — REPLACES the
-- original "redundant-by-construction, F8" safety narrative below with the actual one.
-- F8's implication chain ("a non-empty route symbol implies the graph fact is True") is
-- still literally true, but it undersold what actually holds: `mangledFunDefsPresentRef`
-- is not merely implied True in that case, it is CONSTANT TRUE on every emit path,
-- unconditionally — see `graphCarriesMangledFunDefs`'s header for the mechanism
-- (`private_mangle.mdk:14-16` mangles core's own funDefs unconditionally, before this
-- flag is ever computed; measured ~70 `@mdk_<mid>__*` symbols in a feature-free build's
-- IR with zero shadows).  F8's phrasing hid its own precondition: it is only a
-- meaningful narrowing test if the flag CAN be False on some occurrence's compile, and
-- on the emit path it never is.  The actual safety property is therefore simpler and
-- stronger than "redundant, measured by a negative control": THE FLAG IS CONSTANT TRUE
-- THE MOMENT MANGLING RAN AT ALL, so its conjunct can never be what rejects an
-- occurrence the un-mangled reading of `occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym` would have
-- accepted — the predicate's real discriminator is still, and only, the
-- per-occurrence route symbol.
--
-- 🚨 THIS FACT CURRENTLY HAS NO DISCRIMINATING CONSUMER — L4's conjunct
-- (`mangledFunDefsPresentRef`) is constant-True on emit and its partner
-- (`occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym`) is always-empty off emit.  It is explicit
-- documentation of an implicit invariant, not a live condition.  Do not migrate a
-- reader onto it expecting it to select.  KEPT rather than reverted (owner ruling,
-- RUN-XMOD-045): provably zero-risk, and "this graph was mangled" is more readable
-- than the anonymous `routeLocalSym … /= ""` idiom it replaced, even though it cannot
-- currently narrow anything a build-time `medaka check`/`run`/`build` differential
-- could observe from outside the compiler.
comments.code_after:
importerShadowOnEmitPath : String -> Ref Route -> Bool
importerShadowOnEmitPath name tagRef =
  singleTyparamIfaceMethod name
    && driverState.value.mangledFunDefsPresentRef.value
    && occurrenceCarriesMangledShadowSym name tagRef

-- §2.1 immediates, C → Medaka.  The returned C scalar is re-tagged
-- `(x << 1) | 1`, and the `LTy` follows the DECLARED head so `Bool`/`Char`
-- results print and branch as themselves.
--
-- 🚨 TAGGING ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH FOR `Bool`/`Char` (#2128).  `tagInt` is a
-- faithful re-tag of WHATEVER 63-bit payload C handed back, and for `Int` that
-- is exactly right — every `i64` is a valid `Int`.  `Bool` and `Char` are not
-- like that: their native reps are SUBSETS of the immediate space (§8.1), and a
-- user's C function is under no obligation to stay inside them.  The stdlib
-- predicate externs elsewhere in this file also `tagInt` a raw `r`, but they
-- call OUR OWN C in `runtime/medaka_rt.c`, written to return exactly 0 or 1; a
-- foreign library was never told that contract.  Before this arm normalised,
-- `long long cTruthy(void){ return 42; }` behind `extern cTruthy : Unit ->
-- <FFI "…"> Bool` produced the word 85, which is NEITHER `3` (True) nor `1`
-- (False) — and the two constructs that read a Bool DISAGREED on it: `if`
-- untags and tests `!= 0` (emitIf), so it took the True branch, while `match`
-- compares the immediate word against 3/1 exactly (emitRefutMatch), so it fell
-- off the end into E-NONEXHAUSTIVE-MATCH.  Same program, same value, two
-- answers.  So:
--
--   * `Bool` is NORMALISED, not merely tagged — C's own truthiness rule (0 is
--     false, every other bit pattern is true) is applied at the boundary, which
--     is the convention every C caller already writes to, and the result is one
--     of the exactly two words `if` and `match` both agree about.
--   * `Char` is VALIDATED and TRAPS — see ffiNormalizeChar.
comments.code_after:
ffiEmitCall e fname rty cargs
  | ffiCrossableHead rty =
    let r = freshReg e
    let _ = emit e "  \{r} = call i64 @\{fname}(\{cargs})"
    if rty == "Bool" then
      (ffiNormalizeBool e r, LTBool)
    else if rty == "Char" then
      (ffiNormalizeChar e fname r, LTChar)
    else
      (tagInt e r, ffiImmediateLTy rty)
  | otherwise =
    gapE
      e
      "non-crossable return type '\{rty}' reached the FFI lowering (compiler/FFI-ABI.md section 1)"
comments.note: #2128 named; "Before this arm normalised" resolves to it

-- emit the guard tests left-to-right: a `CGBool` tests a Bool (`True` = the word
-- 3) and branches to `failL` on failure, falling through on success; a
-- `CGBind p <- e` evaluates `e` and refutably matches `p` against it via
-- `emitRefutMatch` (an irrefutable `p` emits no test + just binds; a refutable
-- `Just x <- e` tests the discriminant and branches to `failL` on no-match — G5).
-- Returns the env extended by any `CGBind` bindings (visible to later guards +
-- the body).
comments.code_after:
emitGuardChain : Emit ->
  OrdMap (String, LTy) ->
  List CGuard ->
  CExpr ->
  String ->
  OrdMap (String, LTy)
emitGuardChain _ env [] _ _ = env
emitGuardChain e env ((CGBool g) :: rest) body failL =
  let (bw, _) = emitExpr e env g
  let cmp = freshReg e
  let _ = emit e "  \{cmp} = icmp eq i64 \{bw}, 3"
  let pass = "guardok" ++ intToString (freshLocal e)
  let _ = emit e "  br i1 \{cmp}, label %\{pass}, label %\{failL}"
  let _ = emit e (pass ++ ":")
  emitGuardChain e env rest body failL
emitGuardChain e env ((CGBind p ex) :: rest) body failL =
  let (v, _) = emitExpr e env ex
  let env2 = emitRefutMatch e env p v body failL
  emitGuardChain e env2 rest body failL
